## Pull request overview

Fixes `apps/console` i18n loading to be compatible with the `@objectstack/spec` REST API response envelope so `useObjectLabel` / `useObjectTranslation` receive the actual translation map (restoring non-English business object/field labels).

**Changes:**
- Extracts `loadLanguage` into `apps/console/src/loadLanguage.ts` and unwraps `{ data: { translations } }` when present.
- Updates `apps/console/src/main.tsx` to import and pass the shared `loadLanguage` into `I18nProvider`.
- Adds a new Vitest suite covering envelope unwrapping, flat fallback, and failure/edge cases; updates `CHANGELOG.md`.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 4 out of 4 changed files in this pull request and generated 3 comments.

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| apps/console/src/main.tsx | Switches to importing `loadLanguage` from a dedicated module and wires it into `I18nProvider`. |
| apps/console/src/loadLanguage.ts | Implements spec-envelope detection/unwrap logic with fallback behavior and error handling. |
| apps/console/src/__tests__/LoadLanguage.test.tsx | Adds unit tests for envelope unwrap, fallback behavior, and error cases. |
| CHANGELOG.md | Documents the fix in the Unreleased “Fixed” section. |

These tests trigger `console.warn` in the HTTP error and network failure cases, which will add noise to the test output. Consider stubbing `console.warn` (e.g., via `vi.spyOn(console, 'warn').mockImplementation(() => {})`) for the duration of this test suite and restoring it in `afterEach`/`afterAll`.

This changelog entry says the fix was made in `apps/console/src/main.tsx`, but `loadLanguage` was moved to and updated in `apps/console/src/loadLanguage.ts`. Update the referenced file path to avoid misleading release notes.
```suggestion
- **i18n loadLanguage Not Compatible with Spec REST API Response Format** (`apps/console`): Fixed `loadLanguage` in `apps/console/src/loadLanguage.ts` to correctly unwrap the `@objectstack/spec` REST API envelope `{ data: { locale, translations } }`. Previously, the function returned the raw JSON response, which meant `useObjectLabel` and `useObjectTranslation` hooks received a wrapped object instead of the flat translation map, causing business object and field labels (e.g., CRM contact/account) to fall back to English. The fix extracts `data.translations` when the spec envelope is detected, while preserving backward compatibility with mock/dev environments that return flat translation objects. Includes 6 unit tests covering spec envelope unwrapping, flat fallback, HTTP errors, network failures, and edge cases.
```
